subject: Physics
description: Wave properties — wavelength, frequency, wave speed (v=fλ), transverse vs longitudinal, sound vs light, Doppler effect.

questions.stem: The relation between wave speed (v), frequency (f), and wavelength (λ) is:

options.option_text: v = f / λ (a wrong form here)

questions.explanation: WAVE EQUATION: v = f × λ, where v = wave speed (m/s), f = frequency (Hz = 1/s), λ = wavelength (m). UNIVERSAL: applies to ALL waves — sound, light, water, electromagnetic, seismic. EXAMPLES: (1) SOUND in AIR: v ≈ 343 m/s; if f = 440 Hz (musical note A), λ = 343/440 ≈ 0.78 m. (2) LIGHT in vacuum: v = c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s; visible light frequency ~5 × 10¹⁴ Hz, λ ~600 nm. (3) AM RADIO: 1 MHz, λ = 300 m; FM at 100 MHz, λ = 3 m. KEY DEFINITIONS: WAVELENGTH (λ) = distance between consecutive crests (or troughs); FREQUENCY (f) = cycles per second (Hz); PERIOD (T) = time per cycle = 1/f; AMPLITUDE = max displacement from equilibrium (loudness for sound, brightness for light). RELATIONSHIPS: f × T = 1; v = λ/T; v = f × λ. INSIGHT — different colors of light have DIFFERENT frequencies (and wavelengths) but ALL travel at SAME speed c in vacuum. RED light: λ ~700 nm; violet: λ ~400 nm. RAINBOW: visible spectrum split by prism/raindrops. PYQ FREQUENCY: wave equation v=fλ in NEET, JEE-Main 2-3× per paper, NCERT-driven SSC 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: SOUND waves in air are classified as:
questions.explanation: SOUND in AIR: LONGITUDINAL — particles oscillate ALONG the direction of wave propagation (compressions and rarefactions). MECHANICAL — needs a medium (cannot travel in vacuum). DEFINITIONS: (1) TRANSVERSE WAVES — particles oscillate PERPENDICULAR to wave direction (e.g., light, water waves on surface, EM waves, seismic S-waves). (2) LONGITUDINAL WAVES — particles oscillate PARALLEL to wave direction (e.g., sound, seismic P-waves). (3) MECHANICAL WAVES — need medium (sound, water, seismic, slinky). (4) ELECTROMAGNETIC WAVES — DON'T need medium (light, radio, X-rays — propagate as oscillating electric+magnetic fields). KEY DIFFERENCES: SOUND speed in air ~343 m/s (depends on T, density). SOUND in WATER: ~1,500 m/s (~4× faster). SOUND in STEEL: ~5,100 m/s (~15× faster than air). SOUND in VACUUM: cannot propagate (no particles). SHOUTING ON THE MOON: would be silent — no atmosphere; astronauts use radios. AUDIBLE RANGE: humans hear ~20 Hz to 20,000 Hz (20 kHz). Below 20 Hz = INFRASOUND (elephants, whales communicate with infrasound). Above 20 kHz = ULTRASOUND (bats, dolphins, medical imaging). PYQ FREQUENCY: sound-wave properties in NEET, NCERT, JEE-Main 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: LIGHT waves are EM (electromagnetic) waves and:

options.option_text: Have lowest speed of any wave

questions.explanation: LIGHT (and all EM waves) — TRANSVERSE in nature, can travel through VACUUM. SPEED in VACUUM: c = 299,792,458 m/s ≈ 3 × 10⁸ m/s. KEY: EM waves are oscillating ELECTRIC + MAGNETIC fields propagating perpendicular to each other AND to direction of motion. NO MEDIUM needed (a key 19th-century debate; Michelson-Morley experiment 1887 disproved 'aether'). EM SPECTRUM (low to high frequency / long to short wavelength): RADIO → MICROWAVES → INFRARED → VISIBLE LIGHT (red→violet) → ULTRAVIOLET → X-RAYS → GAMMA RAYS. ALL TRAVEL AT c in vacuum. WAVELENGTHS: radio ~m to km; microwaves ~cm; IR ~µm; visible 400-700 nm; UV ~10-400 nm; X-rays ~0.01-10 nm; gamma < 0.01 nm. EVERYDAY EMISSIONS: (1) Sun — full spectrum. (2) Lightbulb — visible + IR. (3) WiFi — microwaves (~2.4 GHz). (4) X-ray machine — X-rays. SPEED IN MEDIUM: light SLOWS in glass, water (refractive index n; v = c/n). Glass n ~1.5; water n ~1.33; diamond n ~2.4 → light is 2.4× slower in diamond. EINSTEIN's special relativity (1905): c is the universal speed limit; nothing material can travel faster than c. PYQ FREQUENCY: EM wave properties in NEET, JEE-Main 2× per paper.

questions.stem: The DOPPLER EFFECT is observed when:

options.option_text: Source and observer move relative to each other
Wave passes through a denser medium (option here)
Wave reflects off a flat surface (option here)
Two waves combine in same direction (option here)

questions.explanation: DOPPLER EFFECT (Christian Doppler, 1842): apparent CHANGE IN FREQUENCY (or wavelength) observed when SOURCE and OBSERVER are in RELATIVE MOTION. APPROACHING source/observer → frequency INCREASES (shorter wavelength). RECEDING → frequency DECREASES (longer wavelength). EVERYDAY EXAMPLES: (1) AMBULANCE SIREN: pitch HIGHER as it APPROACHES, LOWER as it RECEDES — same physical sound from siren. (2) FORMULA 1 RACING — engine pitch shifts dramatically as cars whiz by. APPLICATIONS: (1) RADAR speed guns — measure vehicle speed via Doppler shift in reflected radio waves. (2) MEDICAL ULTRASOUND — Doppler probes measure blood flow rates. (3) WEATHER RADAR — Doppler radar tracks storm motion. (4) ASTRONOMY — REDSHIFT: galaxies' light shifts to red (longer λ) as they recede; basis for Hubble's discovery (1929) that universe is EXPANDING. (5) BLUESHIFT — galaxies/stars approaching us. KEY FORMULA (sound, source moving): f' = f × v / (v − v_source) — for approaching source. EXAM TIP: 'siren pitch change' is the universal example. IS DOPPLER for LIGHT: yes — relativistic Doppler effect; foundation of cosmology, satellite tracking. PYQ FREQUENCY: Doppler effect in NEET, JEE-Main 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: The frequency RANGE of AUDIBLE sound for humans is approximately:
questions.explanation: HUMAN AUDIBLE RANGE: ~20 Hz (lowest, deep bass) to ~20,000 Hz (highest, very high pitch). DECLINES WITH AGE (PRESBYCUSIS): adults' upper limit drops to ~12-15 kHz by age 30-40; high-frequency hearing loss is universal with aging. INFRASOUND: < 20 Hz — felt rather than heard (vibrations); whales, elephants, hippos communicate using infrasound (travels far). Used by DEFENSE for long-range comm. ULTRASOUND: > 20 kHz — used by BATS (echolocation, ~20-200 kHz), DOLPHINS, CATS, DOGS (up to ~45 kHz — dog whistles emit at 20-25 kHz, human-inaudible but dogs hear). MEDICAL ULTRASOUND: ~1-20 MHz; pregnancy scans, abdominal scans, echocardiography. PHYSICAL EFFECT: low frequencies reach FAR; high frequencies attenuate over distance (why distant thunder sounds 'rumbly' — high frequencies absorbed). INDIA NOISE STANDARDS (CPCB): residential limits 55 dB day / 45 dB night; commercial 65/55; industrial 75/70; silence zones (near schools/hospitals) 50/40. NOISE POLLUTION: > 85 dB prolonged exposure causes hearing damage. PYQ FREQUENCY: human hearing range in NEET, NCERT-driven SSC GA 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Speed of sound in AIR at room temperature is approximately:
questions.explanation: SPEED OF SOUND in AIR at 20°C and 1 atm: ~343 m/s = ~1235 km/h. AT 0°C: ~331 m/s. AT 100°C: ~387 m/s. INCREASES with TEMPERATURE: roughly v ≈ 331 + 0.6T (T in °C). WHY: warmer air = faster molecular motion = faster transmission of pressure waves. SPEED of SOUND in OTHER MEDIA: (1) FRESH WATER (20°C): ~1480 m/s. (2) SEA WATER: ~1530 m/s (slightly faster due to salinity). (3) STEEL: ~5100 m/s (~15× faster than air). (4) GLASS: ~5500 m/s. (5) DIAMOND: ~12,000 m/s (highest known). REASON: solids are more INCOMPRESSIBLE; sound transmits via pressure waves in atomic lattice. CONTRAST WITH LIGHT: light is much faster (3 × 10⁸ m/s) — that's why we see lightning before hearing thunder. RULE: count seconds between flash and thunder; divide by 3 to estimate distance in km. SUPERSONIC: above speed of sound (Mach 1). MACH NUMBER = velocity / speed of sound. SUPERSONIC AIRCRAFT: Concorde (Mach 2.04), SR-71 Blackbird (Mach 3.3+), HYPERSONIC missiles (Mach 5+). SONIC BOOM occurs when aircraft crosses Mach 1 — pressure waves merge into shock front. PYQ FREQUENCY: sound speed in NEET, NCERT, SSC physics 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: A sound wave has frequency 500 Hz and wavelength 0.7 m in air. The speed is:
questions.explanation: Apply WAVE EQUATION: v = f × λ. Plug: v = 500 × 0.7 = 350 m/s. CONSISTENT with sound in air (typical 343 m/s); slight variation OK due to room T. NUMERICAL CHECK: 500 Hz means 500 cycles/sec. Each cycle has wavelength 0.7 m. So in 1 second, wave covers 500 × 0.7 = 350 m. KEY METHOD: identify which two of (v, f, λ) are given; compute the third. PRACTICE: (1) f = 1000 Hz, λ = 0.34 m → v = 340 m/s (sound in air). (2) v = 1500 m/s (water), f = 600 Hz → λ = 2.5 m. (3) Light: c = 3×10⁸, f = 6×10¹⁴ → λ = 5×10⁻⁷ m = 500 nm (green light). UNIT CHECKS: m/s = (1/s) × m ✓. Always verify units! REAL-WORLD: opera singer hits high C ~1046 Hz; air wavelength ~0.33 m; double bass low E ~41 Hz; air wavelength ~8.4 m. INSIGHT — INSTRUMENTS: long instruments (organ pipes, double bass) produce LOW frequencies (long wavelengths fit better); short instruments (piccolo, violin) high frequencies. PYQ FREQUENCY: simple v=fλ calculations 2-3× per JEE-Main, NEET; 1× per SSC CGL Tier 2.
